parameters.name: n_targets
parameters.description: Number of target parts in the bombing operation

parameters.name: target_distance
parameters.description: Airport distance for each target part

parameters.name: destruction_probability
parameters.description: Destruction probability when using bomb type k against target part i

parameters.name: bomb_stock
parameters.description: Available stock for each bomb type

parameters.name: loaded_flight_efficiency
parameters.description: Loaded-flight efficiency for each bomb type

parameters.name: minimum_destroyed_targets
parameters.description: Minimum number of target parts that must be destroyed for mission success

variables.name: attack_assignment
variables.description: Binary decision indicating whether target part i is attacked with bomb type k

variables.name: optimal_success_probability
variables.description: Maximum achievable probability that at least m target parts are destroyed

constraints.name: single_bomb_per_sortie
constraints.description: Each sortie carries exactly one bomb and is assigned to at most one target part, so each selected (i,k) pair represents one bomb use

constraints.name: attack_assignment_binary
constraints.description: Binary decision variables for assigning target part i to bomb type k

constraints.name: one_bomb_type_per_target
constraints.description: Each target part can be attacked with at most one bomb type

constraints.name: bomb_stock_limit
constraints.description: The number of bombs of each type used across all selected target parts cannot exceed available stock

constraints.name: fuel_budget_limit
constraints.description: The total fuel consumed by all selected sorties, including loaded-flight, empty-aircraft, and sortie overhead components, cannot exceed the total fuel budget

objectives.name: mission_success_probability_maximization
objectives.description: Maximize the probability that at least m target parts are destroyed

final_objective.description: Maximize the mission success probability surrogate represented by the scalar variable P^{\star}. No exact algebraic probability-composition formula is provided in the problem data, so the MILP objective remains a direct maximization of the reported success-probability variable.
